text:
Predicates:
WorksInStudentJobs(x) ::: x works in student jobs on campus.
OrderTakeout(x) ::: x orders takeout frequently in college.
EnjoysDiningHall(x) ::: x enjoys the dining hall meals and recipes.
PickyEater(x) ::: x is a picky eater.
SpendsTimeInDiningHall(x) ::: x spends a lot of their time eating and catching up with friends in the campus dining halls.
NeedsMoney(x) ::: x needs to earn money to help pay for college tuition.
Hannah ::: Hannah
MarysSchool(x) ::: x is at Mary's school.

Premises:
∀x (WorksInStudentJobs(x) → NeedsMoney(x)) ::: If people at Mary's school work in student jobs, then they need to earn money.
∀x (OrderTakeout(x) → WorksInStudentJobs(x)) ::: If people order takeout frequently, then they work in student jobs.
∀x (OrderTakeout(x) ∨ (EnjoysDiningHall(x) ∧ Recipes(x))) ::: People order takeout frequently or enjoy the dining hall meals and recipes.
∀x (EnjoysDiningHall(x) → ¬PickyEater(x)) ::: If people enjoy the dining hall meals, then they are not picky eaters.
∀x (EnjoysDiningHall(x) → SpendsTimeInDiningHall(x)) ::: If people enjoy the dining hall meals, then they spend a lot of their time in the dining halls.
Hannah ::: Hannah.
WorksInStudentJobs(Hannah) ::: Hannah works in student jobs.
(NeedsMoney(Hannah) → (¬PickyEater(Hannah) ∧ NeedsMoney(Hannah))) ::: If Hannah needs to earn money, then she is not picky and needs to earn money.

Conclusion:
NeedsMoney(Hannah) ::: Hannah needs to earn money to help pay for her college tuition.
